N° 16Civic-education and deliberation platform on land and citizenship2026

Terre, Peuples & République

A civic-education platform that separates four questions confused in Cameroonian political debate (a people’s history, the development of land, the legal status of a plot and citizenship) and examines each against the Constitution, the land texts of 1974 and 1976 and dated scholarship.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem statement

Before the 2026 local elections, the slogan “Le Littoral aux Littoraliens” called for elected offices in the Littoral region to be reserved for people whose families originate there. The debate that followed treated administrative regions as ethnic property and land rights as a matter of ancestry, while the legal provisions that do refer to origin were either concealed or stretched. Few participants could check what the law, the land registry and historians actually say.

02

Contribution

A long-form text and two opinion pieces state the thesis: no Cameroonian is a stranger in their own country, and arriving first, or meeting the colonial power first, confers no additional political right. Each module then lets the visitor test the claim. A timeline separates oral tradition, documented fact and law. A map compares the seven provinces of 1972 with the ten-unit division in force since 1983. A land laboratory examines nine plots, from a titled house to a forest reserve, asking each time whether the owner’s origin changes anything. A simulation turns bush into a town, after which a decree draws a new region and no plot changes hands. A test shows that the law never defines who is autochthonous. A fact checker corrects claims from both sides, and a counter-argument page states the opposing case at its strongest and invites a vote.

03

Architecture

Preact behind a React-compatible interface keeps the bundle small on mobile networks, with TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind and d3-geo for the maps. The forum and the votes run on Supabase Postgres with row-level security: visitors may read and post but never edit or delete, a trigger limits flooding, and three reports hide a message automatically.

04

Method and data

Libre Arbitre, the debate agent, answers extreme statements from a verified knowledge base executed in the browser, combining a fact, the relevant law and a question in return. An optional generative mode runs in a Supabase Edge Function with rate limits and remains disabled until a key is configured. Every factual statement is tied to one of the 39 dated sources.

05

Verification and limitations

The site states plainly what it could not verify, and its simulations are labelled as fictional. It is an independent citizen initiative with no party or community affiliation; its thesis is argued openly, and the opposing case is given at full strength.
